access.edition_or_version: Clay Sanskrit Library edition translated by Somadeva Vasudeva

mechanics.premise: A king weds an ascetic maiden in secret, forgets her under an ascetic curse, and can only remember her upon recovering a lost signet ring.
mechanics.reader_promise: Exquisite progression of romantic longing, painful separation, and cosmic reconciliation governed by Sringara rasa.
mechanics.opening: King Dusyanta pursues a deer into Kanva's sacred hermitage; dramatic intrusion of regal desire into ascetic sanctuary.
mechanics.point_of_view: Classical multi-tier dramatic staging alternating between Sanskrit royal speech and Prakrit feminine dialogue.
mechanics.character_system: Dusyanta (hero/nayaka), Sakuntala (heroine/nayika), Anasuya and Priyamvada (intimate companions), Durvasas (curse catalyst).
mechanics.conflict_and_stakes: Sacred duty (dharma) versus emotional passion (kama); catastrophic loss of memory and legitimacy.
mechanics.structure: Seven-act nataka architecture progressing from hermitage desire to court repudiation to celestial reconciliation.
mechanics.scene_movement: Shifts between idyllic forest, royal court, and heavenly realm (Marica's hermitage).
mechanics.dialogue: Lyrical verse stanzas interspersed with realistic comedic and dramatic prose.
mechanics.setting: Malini riverbanks, Hastinapura royal court, celestial ashram on Hemakuta mountain.
mechanics.style_and_devices: Dhvani (suggestion), ring-composition motif, token of recognition (abhijnana), pathetic fallacy.
mechanics.emotional_progression: Sambhogasringara (love in union) -> vipralambhasringara (love in separation) -> karuna (sorrow) -> shanta/ananda (peace).
mechanics.suspense_or_anticipation: Audience knows of the curse and the lost ring while Sakuntala and Dusyanta remain trapped by forgetfulness.
mechanics.climax: Act V court rejection where Dusyanta denies knowing pregnant Sakuntala because the ring was lost in Sachi pilgrimage pool.
mechanics.ending: Reunion in Act VII when Dusyanta discovers his son Sarvadamana playing with a lion cub; recognition confirmed by unyielding amulet.
mechanics.conventions: Conforms strictly to Natyashastra nataka rules: royal hero, noble heroine, supernatural curse, auspicious denouement.
mechanics.innovation_or_subversion: Softens Mahabharata original by introducing the curse of Durvasas to protect both lovers' moral integrity.
mechanics.critical_reception: Acclaimed globally by Goethe, William Jones, and centuries of Indian aesthetic theorists as masterwork of classical Sanskrit drama.
mechanics.audience_reception: Definitive cultural emblem of romantic longing, separation, and divine reunification.
